articles.title: Psylocke Proves She's the X-Men's Best Leader by Doing Something She Once Couldn't
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Psylocke has gone through a lot of changes in her career with the X-Men, and she proved during DNX that she has changed in unexpected ways. Before Cyclops headed in to face off with the Chairman and attempt to save the world, he left Psylocke in charge of his X-Men team. She didn't know why […]
articles.content:
In X-Men #41 (2026) by Jed MacKay and Netho Diaz, Psylocke proved to herself and to the rest of the team that she was not an assassin anymore. She was a hero, and she proved this by not giving in to her impulses when she knew it would hurt all mutants. She was also able to save the day outside the area where Cyclops was trying to save the world against the Chairman.

Cyclops went in alone to fight the Chairman, and Psylocke was left in charge of the X-Men . She said they needed to follow his orders, which meant stopping the forces wanting to frame the team for the Chairman's actions. In this situation, the X-Men had strong allies with the Fantastic Four, who had saved Magneto's life and were helping to stop the biological warfare that the Chairman and his team had set into motion. Psylocke then barked out the orders and then sent part of the team into action against O*N*E (the Office of National Emergency), the government's task force that has strong anti-mutant leanings.

O*N*E showed up to arrest them, and while Psylocke told them they needed help working together, they also knew that Frank Bohannan (the former Crimson Commando) only wants to kill all mutants. This didn't go over well with the Invisible Woman, and the fight was on. Bohannan vocally blamed the X-Men for what happened, and the Human Torch was shocked before Magneto said that O*N*E wanted to scapegoat them because 3K was defeated. This would help Bohannan gain more favor, and he could eliminate the mutants he hates the most.

When the fight started, Psylocke barked out one order, and that was “No one dies.” She even emphasized this to Magneto, who agreed to follow her orders and just ground the fighter planes that were firing on them. The battle then came down to Bohannan and Psylocke one-on-one. Bohannan tried to kill her, but Psylocke fought back and finally took down the head of O*N*E. Bohannan admitted that his mutant powers gave him the advantage over Psylocke, but she then revealed that she is just like Cyclops. It's not her powers that make her dangerous. When Bohannan said he would kill her, she took him down and said it was time for him to die. However, she didn't kill him.

This was the most important part of this story because she chose not to kill him. Bohannan told her that if she killed him, a government official, it would destroy the X-Men. He said that if she killed him, the government would drone-strike Alaska and then take out the X-Men in Louisiana. He said that if she killed him, mutants everywhere would die. When the Invisible Woman said that he attacked one of the country's most beloved teams in the Fantastic Four, Bohannan said that the events in Symkaria ( from Avengers Armageddon ) were already turning the public against all heroes, including the Fantastic Four.

Psylocke knew that killing Bohannan would be a mistake, and she also never planned to kill him anyway. Psylocke said that the mutants were ready for a war, and even though Bohannan said the United States would win every war eventually, she pulled back. The Invisible Woman then showed why she is so dangerous. She told Bohannan that he was a madman who deserved to be put away, and then said his job was to quarantine and help fix things, and he wasn't doing his job. He left and threatened the entire Fantastic Four as he did, but he called off the attacks and cleared the X-Men of the attacks.

However, what happened next was chilling. Psylocke said that Bohannan's position couldn't protect him forever and that something had to be done. The Invisible Woman then said the one line that should put Bohannan and anyone like him in fear. She said men like Bohannan have to be handled privately, quietly, invisibly. Susan Richards is a genuine hero, but this sounds like she understands that something has to be done to Bohannan in a manner where no one knows who did it. It sounds like O*N*E just made a very dangerous enemy.

What are your thoughts about Psylocke's transformation throughout the years in Marvel Comics? Let us know your favorite Psylocke moments in the comments below.

articles.title: SAG-AFTRA Drops Thousands of Members for Not Paying Dues as Internal Tensions Rise
articles.summary: Colton Little has had recurring roles on “Days of Our Lives” and “General Hospital,” and was a guest star on “NCIS Origins.” This month, he became one of thousands of SAG-AFTRA members who were terminated by the union because he did not pay his dues. “I fell behind on my dues over a year ago,” […]
articles.content:
Colton Little has had recurring roles on "Days of Our Lives" and "General Hospital," and was a guest star on "NCIS Origins." This month, he became one of thousands of SAG-AFTRA members who were terminated by the union because he did not pay his dues.

"I fell behind on my dues over a year ago," he tells Variety , saying he owes about $2,000. "I was going through a lot. It got to the point where I had to prioritize paying my dues or paying my rent." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Disney Quarterly Revenue Rises 16% and Profit Doubles; Company Forecasts $3 Billion in Annual Cost Savings by 2029 Including Through Layoffs Disney+ and Hulu App Merger Slated to Be Complete in December

He is far from alone. For the last six years, SAG-AFTRA has refrained from kicking out members who fall behind on their dues, given how hard it has been for actors to find work during a pandemic, multiple strikes and a severe downturn in production.

But on Nov. 1, the union reimposed its pre-COVID policy that anyone who falls behind by 18 months or more will be terminated. That decision, made by the board more than a year ago, has contributed to an atmosphere of discontent among some members. Another factor is the board decision last month to extend the contract of Duncan Crabtree-Ireland , the union's national executive director, for four years and to give him a 15% raise.

Crabtree-Ireland was already the highest-paid union official in Hollywood, with a salary of $1.1 million. For some, the timing of the extension — just a few days before thousands of members were kicked out — was a bad look.

"It just feels like, OK, he gets a boost while we get booted," says Taji Coleman, who was threatened with termination but has since resolved her dues issue.

Crabtree-Ireland's contract was not due to expire until June 2028. Sean Astin, the union president, defended the decision to act now as a "bold move." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Negotiating Duncan's contract early and securing his services for an extended period of time is a sign of strength and stability," Astin said, adding that the deal was approved by the union's finance and executive committees before going to the full board at an in-person meeting. "The fact that the union was not in the middle of a major negotiation or an internal election cycle created a healthy space to evaluate such a consequential decision."

The sole "no" vote on the contract, Peter Antico, ran unsuccessfully for secretary-treasurer in 2025 and has been a longstanding critic of union leadership.

"I wanted to fire him," Antico tells Variety . "I'm not in favor of giving this guy money."

Chuck Slavin, who ran unsuccessfully for president last year, argued that the union needs "change at the top."

"SAG-AFTRA is in a full-blown crisis of confidence, driven by the removal of thousands of members, a disturbing lack of financial transparency, disastrous contract decisions, growing threats to pension and healthcare security, inadequate AI protections and leadership that has become increasingly disconnected from the very members it is supposed to serve," Slavin said.

Crabtree-Ireland has sought to stay out of the internal political fray, which will get more intense as the union heads into its election season next spring. Extending his deal now gives him some assurance that his tenure will not depend on the outcome of that vote.

In an interview, Crabtree-Ireland declined to comment on his contract, preferring to leave that to others. But he did address concerns about member terminations, healthcare, and other issues confronting the union.

"The industry is in this moment right now where people are very anxious because of the downturn in production and what's gone on with Warner Bros. and Paramount," Crabtree-Ireland says. "There's a lot of general anxiety that people are feeling in this, making (the terminations) even more nerve-wracking."

SAG-AFTRA members pay 1.575% of their covered earnings in dues. The union is unusual in that members who are not working can remain active, so long as they pay $246 a year in "base dues." Some members may not have worked in decades. But Crabtree-Ireland argues that it's important for the union's finances for members to pay something. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I think members who are paying dues want there to be that fairness to it," he says.

The slowdown has also caused many actors to lose their union health insurance. In recent months, Drake Bell and Heather Matarazzo posted about being unable to qualify, while Cheyenne Jackson launched a campaign to help actors who are "one job away" from meeting the threshold.

The earnings threshold is set to rise to $28,933 in January. The vast majority of SAG-AFTRA members do not make enough from acting to qualify for coverage. As members lose insurance, many are forced into the individual marketplace, where premiums are far more expensive and are rising fast, partly due to cuts in federal support.

That, in turn, has led to frustration with the union.

"I believe the main reason this is happening now is because of the downturn in work, not because of any changes to the health plan or eligibility," Crabtree-Ireland says, noting that the earnings threshold is rising 3%.

Little, who was among those terminated from the union this month, says he ended up working multiple side jobs to make ends meet. When he realized he was about to lose his membership, he reached out to the union multiple times to try to work out some dues arrangement.

"I was treated with almost an indifference when I called one time," he says. "It felt so frustrating."

He does not bear the union any ill will, he says.

"I understand the need to pay dues," he says. "There's also a reality. They have to take into account the struggles their members are facing."

On Oct. 31, he posted a video on Instagram in the style of a "get ready with me" makeup tutorial.

"Get ready with me to get kicked out of SAG-AFTRA," he said in the video, going on to explain the dire circumstances facing L.A. actors. "There are no auditions. There are no parts. There is nothing filming in L.A. It's really bleak … After a lot of introspection, I've decided to pull back. I've decided not to pay my dues."

The video was meant as an update for his friends, but it resonated with a wider group of actors facing the same crossroads.

"It's not that I'm done with acting," he tells Variety . "I'm an artist and an actor. I love the whole process. At the same time, I think I feel just like I need to take a breath."

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Will Reveal More of Korra's Fate in Season 2
articles.summary: Courtesy of Paramount+ Avatar: Seven Havens began to scratch the surface of what led Korra to destroying the world with the cataclysm, and one of the producers behind the series has confirmed that fans will see more of Korra and what led to this post-apocalyptic event in the second season. Avatar: Seven Havens is quickly speeding our way […]
articles.content:
Avatar: Seven Havens is now in the works on returning for Season 2, and executive producer Sehaj Sethi recently took part in a Reddit AMA and answered all sorts of fan questions about the now in the works season. With Korra first seen in the vision that Pavi and Nisha had about the past , Sethi confirmed that fans will see even more of Korra in the new season and ultimately find out more of what led Korra to seemingly to enact the cataclysm.

When asked about some of the other characters' backstories fans might get to see in the coming season, Sethi confirmed that there are indeed going to be more of them on the way, “Throughout the entire series we try to take peeks into virtually all of our characters’ pasts,” Sethi began before revealing that we'll see much more of Korra , “Book Two will definitely share more about Korra, and what happened during the Cataclysm.” This is also going to open up the series to potentially even more updates about fan-favorite characters too.

Avatar: Seven Havens takes place over 200 years following The Legend of Korra , and because of that Sethi explains that the team, “didn’t make it a priority to try and focus on descendents from characters of the previous series,” because of such a wide time gap between the shows. But it's not impossible to get an update, however, as Sethi further teases fans “will hear about a few of them in flashbacks!” Which means this coming season is going to be very important to putting together the rest of this puzzle for Korra's fate after her series.

In a recent interview with IGN, Sethi also confirmed that more of Korra and Asami's future after The Legend of Korra will be seen in Avatar: Seven Havens Season 2, with Asami confirmed long dead by the time of the new series. They had been seen in a “mover” revealing that Korra and Asami potentially got married following the end of that series. But with more of their future needing to be revealed in the coming season, and that likely leading to a gap that gets Korra to the point of the cataclysm, there's a long amount of time needing to be accounted for.

As Pavi began to tap into the power of her chakras, she also seemed to get more of a connection to Korra in the process. It's been confirmed that Pavi has yet to reconnect to the Avatar Cycle, but it's still possible for that connection to be reformed once more. Especially if there might be future series with future Avatars to explore in the coming years. But what are you hoping to see from Korra in Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ future? Let us know all of your thoughts about in the comments.

articles.title: Penn & Teller Join Short Film 'The Inspector' as "Executive Magic Producers" (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The Spanish short is written and directed by Jandro, one of Spain's biggest magician acts.
articles.content:
Penn & Teller have pulled off their newest trick, coming on board Spanish short film The Inspector as its "executive magic producers."

The move puts the pair in league with Spanish magician, filmmaker and television personality Jandro, who wrote, directed, and produced the dark comedy thriller, which is seeking to become an Oscar contender this awards season. The parties already worked together when Janto appeared on pair's magic competition series Fool Us .

Penn and Teller will now lend their support and name for the movie's awards campaign. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV The CW Sets Biggest-Ever Summer Lineup With 11 Series TV Alyson Hannigan Joins 'Penn & Teller: Fool Us' as Host

Inspector , set in Spain, tells the story of a fraudulent gas inspector who targets vulnerable elderly people, exploiting their trust to gain access to their homes and steal their valuables. His next victim is Carmen, a sweet grandmother with a collection of valuable antiques. He soon gets more than he bargained for. The 12-minute, genre-bending short film combines thriller, mystery and dark comedy.

"Jandro, like Hitchcock, understands cinematic sleight of hand. The Inspector is my kind of movie," said Teller in a statement. "If you like Penn & Teller, you'll love The Inspector. It's tricky.”

Jandro is one of Spain's most well-known magicians and one of the most recognizable faces in Spanish television, having spent 15 years as a writer and performer on the popular Spanish late-night show El Hormiguero. He earned fame in magic circles by hoodwinking Penn & teller as part of their Fool Us competition series. He won that contest six times. articles.title: Emergency Broadcast System Test Still On For Today, Homeland Security Says
articles.summary: Despite a series of technology outages the past week on email systems, aviation communications, airlines, banks, national security networks, and more, the Federal Emergency Management Agency says the long scheduled test today of the Emergency Broadcast System will go ahead. "This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency […]
articles.content:
Despite a series of technology outages the past week on email systems, aviation communications, airlines, banks, national security networks, and more, the Federal Emergency Management Agency says the long scheduled test today of the Emergency Broadcast System will go ahead.

“This is a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System, issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency,” the one-minute long message will states, FEMA said. “This is only a test. No action is required by the public.”

Set to hit at 11:20 a.m. PT/2:30 p.m. ET, the test will appear on “radio and television broadcasters, cable systems, satellite radio and television providers and wireline video,” notes the Department of Homeland Security . According to FEMA , there will be a brief interruption, but “No blackouts, no secret emergencies” connected to the test. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); } Related Stories News Senator's Letters Offer Preview Of Democrats' Plans To Investigate FCC, Big Tech And Perhaps Big Mergers News FCC's Sole Democrat Calls On Broadcast Lobby To Push Back On Trump-Backed Chairman's Regulatory Threats Over Election Coverage

FYI – FEMA falls under the jurisdiction of the DHS.

"During an emergency, every second is crucial," FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton said in a statement Monday. "FEMA's alert and warning systems ensure that no second is wasted getting you the critical information needed to keep you safe. Operational tests, like the one to be conducted tomorrow, allow us to identify and fix potential issues before an actual emergency occurs."

As you might recall from 2023, the feds are obliged by the IPAWS Modernization Act of 2015 to conduct a EAS test every three years. A more localized test of today's test took place in Alaska with no problems.

A further safeguard is in place that if today's test encountered difficulties. FEMA explained back in September: “If an actual emergency or significant weather event occurs on test day, FEMA and the FCC may postpone the test. The backup date for the nationwide test is December 3, 2026.”

articles.title: 'The Odyssey' to Receive Ensemble Performance Award at Palm Springs International Film Festival (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Cast members Matt Damon, John Leguizamo and Samantha Morton as well as casting director John Papsidera are expected to attend the ceremony.
articles.content:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey will receive the Ensemble Performance Award at the Palm Springs International Film Festival , the Palm Springs International Film Awards announced on Tuesday.

Cast members Matt Damon , John Leguizamo and Samantha Morton , as well as casting director John Papsidera, are expected to attend the ceremony. The Film Awards will take place on Jan. 7, 2027, with the festival running from Jan. 7-18.

The Ensemble Performance Award recognizes the “casting director in alignment with the Academy's newly established best casting award.” Previous recipients include Conclave (2025), King Richard (2022), Mary Poppins Returns (2019), Hidden Figures (2017), The Big Short (2016), The Imitation Game (2015), American Hustle (2014), Argo (2013), The Social Network (2011) and Babel (2007). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music Ella Langley Brings Country Into The Grammys' General Field With Seven Nominations Music Grammy Nominations Snubs and Surprises: Harry Styles, Madonna, Noah Kahan Miss Top Nods as Raye, Rosalía Overperform

" The Odyssey is one of the most ambitious films ever made, and its ensemble of performances is nothing short of extraordinary," Festival chairman Nachhattar Singh Chandi says. "From Matt Damon's weathered turn as the hero Odysseus, to Samantha Morton's captivating and terrifying portrayal of Circe, to John Leguizamo's faithful guidance as Eumaeus, these are just a few of the many performances that bring this world of antiquity to vivid, undeniable life. It is a privilege to celebrate this remarkable company of actors and the casting director who brought them together with the Ensemble Performance Award."

The Odyssey was the first feature film to be entirely shot in Imax. It also stars Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Lupita Nyong'o, Jon Bernthal, Charlize Theron and Elliot Page, among others. Nolan wrote and directed the script and produced alongside Emma Thomas. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.title: This Week's FBI Had A Surprising Update, And I Needed To Know About A Potential Spinoff

Shantel VanSanten returned to FBI as Special Agent Nina Chase in Monday’s episode, “Posterity,” which marked her second appearance on the series since FBI: Most Wanted ’s cancellation in 2025. Her return came just a couple of weeks after it was revealed that Nina had been offered a job to lead her own task force in San Diego, leading Scola (John Boyd) to question the logistics of their relationship and raising their son, Dougie. As Nina continued to pack and get in one last case at 26 Fed, Scola was still wrestling with how they were going to make things work. Ultimately, he told Nina he was going to put in a transfer and follow her to San Diego, meaning another FBI exit could be looming .

FBI has been growing as a franchise, like any Dick Wolf series, so it’s totally logical to wonder about a spinoff coming from this update. Having two fan-favorite characters moving across the country for the job would certainly be a missed opportunity for another series, in my humble opinion. While it sounds like there aren’t any plans, and Boyd seems to be sticking around on FBI for the time being, if VanSanten has her way, we very well could be getting a Scolina spinoff at some point in the future. While we wait and hope for that, I'm just glad that it seems like Nina is finally getting closure .

articles.title: One Year Later, My Dress-Up Darling Still Leaves Fans Hanging With No Season 3
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of CloverWorks My Dress-Up Darling wrapped up its second season with an ending that seemed like it was ending the anime overall, and a little over a year later fans have still been left hanging with their hopes of a potential third season ever happening. The anime adaptation for Shinichi Fukuda's original manga series breathed an entirely […]
articles.content:
My Dress-Up Darling ended its second season run last year, but there was still quite a bit of the manga's story left to adapt . This had fans wondering whether or not the series would return for a possible third season, but unfortunately a year later that has yet to be revealed. It seems even further off than that because not only did the second season have an original ending, but those behind the production team touted how there were no plans at the time either.

My Dress-Up Darling Season 2 wrapped up its run with an original scene not seen in Shinichi Fukuda's original manga . Following the end of the group cosplay seen with the Coffin Arc, Marin had fully realized her feelings and accepted that she really was in love with Gojo. She had planned to confess, but decided at the end of the season to instead ask for a selfie together with him as the series came to an end. Which also seemed to be set up to be a potential original anime finale as the two characters were closer than ever.

Producer behind the series, Shota Umehara, had revealed at the time that he would like to pursue a future for the series, but at the time production was a “blank slate” with nothing planned. This not only meant that no potential third season had been decided at the time, but also meant that any continuation would be much further off than fans would likely hope for. Now that we're a year out from the second season, it likely means an even longer wait for a continuation. If one happens at all, anyway. But there's still material left to adapt if the team wanted.

My Dress-Up Darling still has about two arcs of the manga left for a potential anime future with about 30 or so chapters that could be tackled in a third season. This would be a little over the 20 or so chapters adapted with the second season , and that gives plenty of runway for an anime adaptation. There's also a potential to bring the franchise back with a finale movie given that it's a route that many franchises go these days with their respective finale, but it would miss out on all the potential material left on the cutting room floor in that way.

A full third season is really the only way to bring My Dress-Up Darling back, but it's likely going to be quite a while before that happens. CloverWorks has been very busy with all sorts of other projects now at various stages of development, and despite Marin's popularity , finishing off the anime likely isn't at the top of any list at the moment. Given that some franchises have had fans waiting a decade in between potential season before returning, all fans can do right now is wait.

In the meantime, you can catch up with My Dress-Up Darling now streaming with Crunchyroll. Would you want to see it come back with a third season or even a movie someday? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

In a new post on the official PlayStation Blog , San Diego Studio's Ramone Russell reflected on the past year before outlining some of the plans for 2027. Russell acknowledged that the studio needs to improve how it communicates with players and responds to community feedback, suggesting that the developer is looking to address some of the concerns raised throughout the latest release.

Players who aren't ready to move on from MLB The Show 26 will also have another incentive to keep playing. Now & Later Packs are returning, allowing Diamond Dynasty players to earn items for the current game alongside vouchers that can be redeemed for The Show Packs in MLB The Show 27 . However, players must use the same account across both games to receive their rewards.

articles.title: Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse Needs to Do Something the First Two Movies Never Could
articles.summary: Miles Morales has a problem. He's finally figured out that being Spider-Man means making your own rules, only now he's stuck in a universe where practically everybody wants to tell him what those rules should be. Miguel O'Hara thinks he knows how Miles' story is supposed to end. His parents are in danger, the Spider-Society […]
articles.content:
There's also something bigger at stake. The first two movies established Miles as a Spider-Man who could stand alongside Peter Parker without having to imitate him. But Beyond the Spider-Verse has an opportunity to take that idea somewhere neither film could. Miles could finally become a Spider-Man whose adventures don't depend on crossing between dimensions or meeting another version of himself. He needs an ending that feels earned, but I don't think that means Sony should close the door on his future. In fact, the opposite might be considerably more exciting.

One of the best things about Across the Spider-Verse is that it takes the idea of Miles being an anomaly and turns it into something much more personal. Miguel O'Hara believes certain events have to happen for the multiverse to survive. Miles refuses to accept that his father's death should be one of them. That's a pretty enormous disagreement when the person making the rules is leading an army of Spider-People. But Miguel's obsession with preserving canon also creates an interesting contradiction. Spider-Man has always been about people making difficult choices when the odds are against them. Peter Parker didn't become a hero because somebody handed him a list of acceptable tragedies. Miles shouldn't have to either. The first movie established that anybody can wear the mask. The sequel pushed that idea further by showing how much pressure comes with being the person who wears it differently. Now the third installment needs to prove that Miles can make his own choices even when the consequences are enormous.

I'd also hate to see the movie get so caught up in explaining the multiverse that it forgets about the people who make Miles' story worth watching. His relationship with his parents has always been one of the strongest parts of these films. Jefferson and Rio aren't just supporting characters waiting for their son to finish saving reality. They're the reason Miles wants to become a better Spider-Man in the first place. Then there's Gwen, whose relationship with Miles became considerably more complicated after the events of the second movie. The franchise has spent so much time introducing alternate Spider-People and exploring different dimensions that it would be easy to lose sight of its emotional center. Miles doesn't need to defeat Miguel just to prove a philosophical point. He needs to save the people he loves without sacrificing the person he's become. That's a much better ending.

Here's where things get particularly interesting. Miles has spent two movies surrounded by different versions of Spider-Man, but he has never really needed them to justify his place in the franchise. That's why I'd be interested in seeing what happens after the Spider-Verse story ends. The MCU has already established that Miles exists somewhere in its larger universe. Aaron Davis mentioned his nephew in Spider-Man: Homecoming , and Donald Glover returned as the character in Across the Spider-Verse . That was a pretty amusing connection for fans who have been waiting to see Miles make his live-action debut. It also leaves an obvious possibility sitting on the table. What happens when Miles finally gets to meet the Peter Parker played by Tom Holland? We've seen Miles learn from alternate Spider-Men, but a meeting with the MCU's Peter could be something entirely different. Peter is still figuring out how to rebuild his own life after No Way Home . Miles could enter that world as somebody who has already faced the impossible and survived it.

I wouldn't want Sony to rush that crossover just because audiences keep asking for it. Miles deserves more than becoming another character introduced to keep the MCU moving. The whole point of the animated movies is that he doesn't need to live in Peter Parker's shadow. If Beyond the Spider-Verse gives him a proper conclusion, there's no reason his next adventure couldn't take place somewhere completely different. He could become the Spider-Man of his own world without needing another multiverse crisis to make his existence interesting. And that's what makes this final chapter such an appealing opportunity. Sony can finish the story it started in 2018 while leaving Miles with an enormous future ahead of him. I want to see him get home, save his family, and finally decide what being Spider-Man means on his own terms. If that eventually leads him to the MCU, great. But I'd rather see Miles Morales become a hero who can carry his own franchise than another Spider-Man waiting for a crossover.

(Image credit: NBC) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter We’re only a few days away from the Traitors: New Blood finale, and I’m willing to admit the obvious. This has not been the best season of The Traitors . In fact, you could easily say this has been a below-average season. Fans on social media and those I have talked to in real life seem to all be in agreement on that. There’s a growing consensus that the show needs to change. I think producers are going to listen, though I’m terrified they’re going to misunderstand the why.

The biggest, loudest and most obvious change we’ve gotten this season has been the casting of non-celebrities. The US version of The Traitors has historically relied on reality television personalities to provide the drama and bring their fanbases. This season, NBC decided to move the property from Peacock to network television and cast it like a more traditional competition show with randoms . It would be easy to just look at that decision and blame all the problems on the newbies, but that’s actually not the right takeaway.

The biggest problem by a very large margin with Traitors: New Blood is the episode runtimes. The show simply does not work in an hour-long time slot on NBC. In theory, the episodes on Peacock are the same length, as they’re typically between an hour and an hour and ten minutes. Because they’re on streaming, however, that runtime is the actual length of each episode. On network television, an hour-long time slot is actually forty-two minutes or so of real content, which isn’t even close to the amount of time the players need to complete one cycle of the game.

That means every single episode, the editors are making an impossible choice. They can either not include one or more major elements of the show (the breakfast, the mission, the roundtable and the turret), they can completely remove all of the strategy scenes that happen between those major elements, or they can drop most of the confessionals where the players talk directly to the camera and tell us their motivations and theories. There is simply no way to get through all of that in forty-two minutes. So, that has left every episode feeling either incomplete because it didn’t make it through a full cycle of the game, or feeling like a highlight video that simply recaps the basics of what happened.

That format and structure are the problem. The runtime is the problem. It’s not the cast. Even with less confessionals and less screentime, we’ve gotten good content from these players. I’m not saying the Traitors: New Blood cast is better than the cast on Big Brother 14 or Survivor: Heroes vs Villains , but there are some breakout personalities here and plenty of likeable, solid characters who have popped and would have looked even better with more of a chance to talk to the camera.

The Traitors Isn’t Going To Fully Work On NBC Until It Makes An Obvious Change Traitors: New Blood's Fruitgate Was My Favorite Episode So Far, And I Feel So Bad For Victor It Took 4 Episodes Of Survivor 51 For Fans To Get Mad At Producers, But I’m Right There With Them Victor is an all-time great Traitors character and should be a reality television mainstay moving forward. He’s electric. I’m personally obsessed with Jay and have had probably ten conversations with people trying to figure out his vibe and what’s going on in his head. It’s not just those two standouts either. There are a half dozen or so other players who play hard and are capable of delivering strong confessionals. Joe, Katie, Tomica, Michael and Shane have all had great moments, and when given a chance, secondary characters like Wyatt, Clyde, Abby, Abbey, Kriste, Ben, Morgan and others have delivered too. They’re just not always getting the screentime because, once again, every episode feels like it’s set on 1.5X speed.

Survivor and The Amazing Race have lengthened their episodes in recent years to help develop the characters and let the episodes breathe more. That’s the obvious solution here for The Traitors . It either needs to move to 90 minutes, or it needs to move back to Peacock. What it absolutely does not need to do is give up on casting newbies. The UK and other countries have had fantastic seasons using randoms , and in an ideal world, it would be a delight to watch Peacock/ NBC switch back and forth between a season with reality stars and a season with plumbers, farmers and firefighters.

I love The Traitors . It’s one of my favorite shows on television, and despite the obvious format issues, I still enjoyed the content we got this season. I’d like to see producers listen to the fan frustration and make a change, but those alterations should be exclusively focused on the format and not on casting.

articles.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Early Rotten Tomatoes Score Continues a Franchise Trend
articles.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is opening in theaters, and the first big screenings for critics and fans are already happening. As such, official reviews for Sunrise on the Reaping are starting to get posted online, and Rotten Tomatoes is pulling them together to get an official aggregate score, letting people know if […]
articles.content:
Based on current scores, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping looks like it will stand alongside most of the Hunger Games movies Francis Lawrence has made. However, it still falls short of the franchise's most critically acclaimed films by a significant margin.

As of writing this, The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping has a Rotten Tomatoes Score of 69%, with more than 50 reviews having been submitted thus far. That puts Sunrise on the Reaping on par with The Hunger Games: Mockingjay Part 1 and Part 2 , which each carry a score of 70%. It is a step up from the previous Hunger Games prequel, The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes , which carries a Rotten Tomatoes score of 64%. That all said, Sunrise on the Reaping ‘s score is still well below the first two Hunger Games films ( The Hunger Games, The Hunger Games: Catching Fire ), which still hold the highest scores with 85% and 90%, respectively.

It's hard (at this point) to imagine any new Hunger Games movie unseating Catching Fire . That second film is where Franchis Lawrence took over the directorial reins and made a sequel film that was much more in line with Lionsgate's and fans' expectations than the first film. Director Gary Ross ( Pleasantville, Big, Seabiscuit ) tried to make an arthouse film out of the first book, with handheld guerrilla-style filming that left fans dizzy, as well as a muted and shadowy color palette that had fans squinting just to see what was happening. When Lawrence delivered a well-shot and lavishly colored sequel, it sparked a whole new wave of interest in the series; the initial “backlash” to Hunger Games being a Battle Royale clone had faded, and franchise star Jennifer Lawrence was stepping into the prime run of her career. It all amounted to the biggest box office earnings of the entire series, with Catching Fire earning $865 million worldwide.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping may not be hitting the same critical heights as Catching Fire , but it does have a shot at being one of the bigger box office takes in the series. Catching Fire was about Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark being dragged back into the Hunger Games for the 75th Anniversary, after they survived the 74th Games. Every 25 years, the Capitol holds a “Quarter Quell” that demands double the number of tributes from each district to compete in the Hunger Games; Sunrise on the Reaping looks back on the 50th Games, the Second Quarter Quell, where Katniss Everdeen's future mentor, Haymitch Abernathy, competed in one of the bloodiest and most savage tournaments ever. The film will reveal how the massive trauma of the 50th Hunger Games (and its aftermath) inspired the rebellion that would finally strike back at the Capitol by turning Katniss Everdeen into the revolutionary figure known as “The Mockingjay.”

In our ComicBook Review, critic Nicole Drum writes, “ The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is a good movie. It’s honestly a very good adaptation of what might be one of the best books in Suzanne Collins’ overall Hunger Games series. Much about the film makes it easily the best-made in the entire franchise, and it truly has some of the best performances as well. But while it is good, it falls just short of greatness. The potential is there; it is just ultimately unrealized, but it still makes for a fitting (presumably) final chapter in the saga.”

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping will be in theaters starting this weekend.

articles.title: Shonen Jump Creator Breaks Silence on Ending Their Series After 5 Years & Teases Epilogue
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Shueisha A major Shonen Jump series has come to an end after five years with its final chapter released this past weekend, and the creator behind it all has broken their silence on the grand finale with a tease of some new materials for after the series came to an end. The year has already seen […]
articles.content:
Witch Watch officially ended its run with Shonen Jump after five years of serialization this past weekend , and Shinohara took to social media to share a special goodbye message with fans to celebrate the grand finale. Noting how they felt like this was the right time to end the series (despite the fact it felt like it could go on for much longer), Shinohara teases that the final volume release of the series will include some special epilogue art set after the grand finale.

読んでくださった方々本当にありがとうございました！ また日常編に戻るだろうと思ってた人には申し訳ないです。 クライマックスを描き終えた後は短く終わりたい性分なのと、一度日常に戻ると楽しくなって終わり時を見失いそうだったので、ここで完結とさせていただきました。 pic.twitter.com/CzUHyXd26S

Witch Watch officially came to an end with the release of Chapter 270 of the series right after its final battle , and Shinohara began their goodbye message by apologizing to those fans who had hoped to see more of the wacky daily life adventures, “Thank you so much to everyone who read it! I’m sorry to those who thought I’d return to the everyday-life chapters.” But as the creator explained, it would have been hard to keep track of when to actually end the series in that case, “Once I finished writing the climax, I wanted to wrap things up quickly, and I was afraid that once I returned to everyday life, I’d get so caught up in it that I’d lose track of when to end it, so I decided to bring the story to a close here.”

But while Witch Watch seemed like it could have been built to run forever, Shinohara noted how it was time to move on, “Honestly, I could keep drawing a manga like Witch Watch forever if I wanted to, so that’s exactly why I feel I need to bring it to a close at some point and move on to my next challenge.” But thankfully, the creator has also teased there will be some final pages for the characters in the final volume releases, “I plan to draw lots of bonus pages for the final volume, including scenes of the characters’ everyday lives after the story ends, so please be sure to pick it up.”

With Witch Watch creator Kenta Shinohara confirming that there will be some additional pages featuring more of the characters after the grand finale, it's a hope that fans will get some of the closure they had been hoping to see that was absent from the final chapter. With it jumping years into the future, yet still teasing all of the group would still be hanging out together, fans were hoping to just see more of the wacky adventures that drew them to the series in the first place.

But this also isn't the end of the Witch Watch franchise as it has now been confirmed that Season 2 of the anime is now in the works for a release in 2027. No concrete release date has been announced for it just yet, but there's plenty to look forward to even if the manga has come to an end. How do you feel about Witch Watch ‘s ending? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson's Batman Future May Already Be Over Before He Was Cast as James Bond
articles.summary: News that Robert Pattinson is officially the next James Bond had DC fans in a frenzy about his potential Batman future. Whenever an actor is locked down into a major franchise with a major pop culture character, it becomes nearly impossible to then become a part of another one, largely just because of scheduling alone. […]
articles.content:
In a report on TheWrap , the trade reveals that Pattinson's time as Batman may be done already thanks to the frequent delays of The Batman: Part II . According to the outlet, “a source with knowledge” of the actor's deal with Warner Bros. revealed that the delays in the sequel movie “allowed Pattinson to slip out from under his contract,” which would have originally locked him down for a third film. Even with this change in Pattinson's contract for Batman, that doesn't necessarily mean that the upcoming sequel will be his final appearance.

Now, is it possible that Pattinson could still play both parts at the same time? Of course. With no contractual obligation to return for a third Batman movie, it's possible that Pattinson's time as the caped crusader could be over, but if The Batman Part II arrives to major success, Warner Bros. could create a new deal for him to return. Daniel Craig was able to make a slew of other blockbusters while playing James Bond, including The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo , Knives Out , and others; even Tom Holland has managed additional blockbuster work between Spider-Man films.

Robert Pattinson was confirmed as the next Batman on May 31, 2019, with his first appearance happening in 2021 with the release of The Batman . Since that point, delays in production of the sequel have resulted in a protracted timeline for the movie, with the sequel now set to arrive on February 18, 2028, nearly seven years later, and a length of time that has aligned with major changes at Warner Bros. two times over.

First, James Gunn and Peter Safran took over at DC Studios back in 2022, inheriting a job where the world considered Pattinson as Batman but where plans for a new DCU cinematic universe called for another actor to take the part and share the screen with David Corenswet's Superman. Though the DCU took off, with some bumps along the way, the second major event to happen in the gap between The Batman sequels was the departure of Gunn and Safran from DC.

Now, the second major change that happened between the films, Skydance has installed former Marvel producer Jeremy Latcham at DC Studios. Though announced over a week ago, Latcham has not opened up in any meaningful way about what his plans for DC on the big screen will be, and if they include Pattinson at all. Suffice to say, it's possible that by taking on James Bond, Pattinson may be signaling that he's putting Batman behind him, but it still can't be ruled out that he might play both characters at the same time.

Ahead of confirmation that Robert Pattinson would be the new Bond, a report revealed that Amazon MGM had given him more favorable conditions compared to the other actors auditioning for the part: just three movies (with a higher salary) compared to a four-movie deal. Hopefully, for Pattinson it doesn't take seven years for his second Bond movie to get made.

articles.title: As Johnny Depp Faces Pirates Of The Caribbean 6 Rumors, Another Star Weighs In On Returning
articles.summary: I'd love to see these characters back aboard the Black Pearl.
articles.content:
Johnny Depp returning to theaters in Ebenezer on the 2026 movie schedule , renewed interest has grown in whether he'll ever play Captain Jack Sparrow again . Producer Jerry Bruckheimer has already confirmed that discussions have taken place about bringing Depp back for Pirates of the Caribbean 6 , although nothing has been officially announced. Now another familiar face from the original movies has weighed in, and I have to admit, this is one reunion I'd love to see happen.

I would absolutely love this. Pintel and Ragetti were two of my favorite supporting characters from the original trilogy, and their ridiculous behavior provided some great comic relief between all the sword fights and increasingly more extravagant set pieces.

Somehow, they survived three movies filled with undead pirates, sea monsters and increasingly complicated betrayals. That's honestly impressive considering how frequently they seemed to have no idea what was going on. While I certainly want to see Johnny Depp return as Jack Sparrow, I think bringing back characters like these could be just as important to making another Pirates movie feel connected to the originals.

Bruckheimer previously confirmed that he's been speaking with Depp about a sixth movie , although the project remains in development. Depp recently suggested he'd be interested in helping give the franchise a proper sendoff, particularly if it meant working with Bruckheimer again.

The partnership will introduce the Miss Dior x Women at Sundance Institute Award, honoring an emerging filmmaker whose work is making an impact on the industry. The recipient will be selected by a committee, with the award recognizing a rising talent whose early work signals a promising career rather than an established body of work.

The partnership also includes the Women at Sundance Institute Miss Dior Momentum Fellowship, which will support six women filmmakers developing their second or third feature films. The year-round program will provide non-recoupable grants, mentorship, professional development opportunities, industry networking and access to Sundance Institute's educational programs and alumni network.

Chanel has maintained a two-decade relationship with the Tribeca Festival, including its Through Her Lens women's filmmaker program, which celebrated its 11th edition in September. Cartier has partnered with the Venice Film Festival since 2021, while Miu Miu has commissioned short films by women directors through its “Women's Tales” series since 2011, regularly presenting new installments at Venice.

The Dior partnership also builds on Sundance Institute's existing efforts to support women in film. Established in 2012, Women at Sundance Institute expanded its fellowship programming in 2018 with the Momentum Fellowship, designed to support filmmakers at pivotal stages of their careers.

articles.title: GTA 6's Lucia Actress Finally Confirmed After Years of Speculation
articles.summary: After many years of speculation surrounding the identity of Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia actress, fans finally have an official name to put to one of the game's two protagonists. Manni L. Perez has been nominated for Best Performance at The Game Awards 2026 for her work in Grand Theft Auto VI, effectively confirming that […]
articles.content:
The reveal came during The Game Awards' nominee announcement on November 17, which included Perez among the five performers nominated for this year's Best Performance award. Her association with Rockstar's upcoming game puts an end to years of fan speculation about who would bring the Lucia character to life.The news is already generating plenty of excitement among fans who have followed the casting mystery for years.

Perez has been one of the most frequently discussed names in conversations about GTA 6 ‘s cast, with fans pointing to similarities between her appearance and voice and the character shown in Rockstar's trailers. Despite the speculation, neither Perez nor Rockstar Games had publicly confirmed the connection, leaving fans to wait for something more definitive.

Rather than Rockstar publishing a cast announcement or Perez addressing the rumors herself, her Best Performance nomination has provided the clearest official connection yet. It's also a significant moment for the actress, whose work on one of the most anticipated video games of all time is now receiving recognition ahead of the game's release.

The nomination places Perez alongside several other performers recognized at this year's ceremony, including Angela Sant'Albano for Resident Evil: Requiem , Liam McIntyre for Wolverine , Patrick Gibson for 007: First Light , and Rahul Kohli for Saros . The category recognizes individual performances in games, making Perez's inclusion a notable acknowledgment of her contribution to Rockstar's latest project.

Rockstar has kept details about GTA 6 ‘s cast remarkably quiet throughout the game's lengthy development. Although Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos have been central to the game's marketing, the studio has largely avoided identifying the actors responsible for bringing its protagonists to life. The secrecy has only encouraged fans to scrutinize every trailer, interview, and potential casting clue for answers.

Perez's nomination finally gives players a concrete name associated with Lucia, even if Rockstar has yet to publish a complete cast list. There is still plenty of interest in discovering who plays Jason and the other characters players will encounter throughout the game, but this is a major piece of the puzzle finally falling into place.

With Grand Theft Auto 6 scheduled to launch on November 19, fans won't have much longer to wait before experiencing Perez's performance for themselves. After years of speculation, it's fitting that the answer arrived through one of gaming's biggest award annoucements.

Disney -controlled pay-TV provider Fubo ended its fiscal year with a dip in subscribers, but record full-year revenue and better-than-expected profits sent its share price surging Tuesday.

The Disney-Fubo transaction closed in October 2025, finalizing a months-long resolution of a landmark antitrust lawsuit. The complaint alleged antitrust violations and a judge sided with Fubo's argument that programmers had engaged in monopolistic behavior.

Alisa Bowen, a longtime Disney streaming executive who was installed as CEO earlier this year , said the relationship with her former company gives Fubo advantages in the areas of cost synergies, ad sales and marketing.

“Leveraging Disney's broad reach is one of the efficient ways to build brand awareness and to reach potential new subscribers,” Bowen told Wall Street analysts during Fubo's quarterly earnings call. articles.title: 'The Odyssey,' 'Dune 3,' 'Michael' and More Top Artisans Honored at Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards
articles.summary: Cinema’s top artisans were honored at the 15th Annual Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards in partnership with Variety on Friday, celebrating the artists whose behind-the-scenes contributions brought some of the world’s biggest films to life. Hosted by actor and comedian Asif Ali, this year’s honorees included the creative teams behind “The Odyssey,” “Dune: Part Three,” […]
articles.content:
Cinema's top artisans were honored at the 15th Annual Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards in partnership with Variety on Friday, celebrating the artists whose behind-the-scenes contributions brought some of the world's biggest films to life.

Hosted by actor and comedian Asif Ali, this year's honorees included the creative teams behind " The Odyssey ," "Dune: Part Three," "The Invite," " Michael ," "Club Kid," "La Bola Negra," "Paper Tiger," "Wicker," "The Debut" and "Wild Horse Nine." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Brandi Carlile's All-Requests Tour Isn't Just a Magnificent Stunt, but an Unusually Moving Transaction Between Performer and Audience: Concert Review

"Dune" director Denis Villeneuve presented the cinematography award to Linus Sandgren, crediting the cinematographer with helping him reimagine the franchise and convincing him to shoot the third installment using an Imax film camera.

"His versatility as a cinematographer is absolutely outstanding. More importantly, Linus is a poet, a very special soul," Villeneuve said in his introduction. "He is a free spirit and one of the most beautiful humans I have ever met. His joy for filmmaking and passion for cinema are incredibly contagious."

In his acceptance speech, Sandgren revealed that he and the creative team partnered with Atlas Lens to develop custom, large-format Imax lenses to help bring a new vision of Arrakis to life. By the time production wrapped, the team had shot on "every single format, from Imax 65mm film to digital to poetic 16mm," as well as black and white film.

"Every format is carefully chosen for the emotions that Denis wanted to evoke in each shot," Sandgren told the audience. "He challenged us to be inventive." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Also honored were Willie Burton, Craig Henighan, Gary A. Rizzo and Kevin O'Connell, the sound team behind "The Odyssey." Matt Damon introduced the sound award, recalling that nearly all the sounds in the film were organic and that he never had to loop a single line of dialogue in post-production.

"There's many people with us behind the scenes: Foley artists, dialogue editors, sound effects editors, assistance, re-recording mixers or re-recording texts," Henighan said. "I just want to thank and give a shoutout to all of them. Everyone behind the scenes really contributed to everything that we did, and we could bring our best."

The costume design award went to Marci Rodgers for her work on "Michael," which was introduced by Jaafar Jackson. As a longtime fan of the musician, Rodgers recalled studying Michael Jackson's artistry from a young age and dreaming of one day designing his costumes.

"As artists, we all know what it means to carry a dream. Michael and I alike must speak it into existence and turn belief into action," Rodgers said. "But believing in that dream also means you have to have the courage to pursue it. So don't give up on your dream, even when it becomes heavy."

Tracee Ellis Ross presented the screenwriting award to Rashida Jones and Will McCormack for "The Invite," joking that the honorees previously dated for only a few weeks. The duo, who have been writing together for nearly 20 years, said they are often drawn to using comedy to ground stories of heartbreak.

"We have found some really hard moments in our lives have also been the funniest, and that's really what drew us to ‘The Invite': These four people in one apartment trying desperately to hold on to love and the people they dreamed they would be, even as their lives they built begin to fall apart,” Jones said. "Because sometimes, the only way through heartbreak is to laugh, and sometimes laughter is what makes it possible to tell the truth."

Diego Quecano received the property master award for "Club Kid," presented by Jordan Firstman. One of the biggest challenges Quecano faced was recreating the textures of the drugs used in the film, particularly 3-MMC, which he ultimately replicated by mixing lactose powder with vitamin D and heating it up in the oven. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"The textures of all the drugs had to be perfect," Firstman told Variety ‘s senior entertainment writer Angelique Jackson on the red carpet. "3-MMC has a very different texture than K and coke. K is saltier, and coke is more powdery."

When asked about the queer representation among the cast and crew of "Club Kid," Quecano told Variety that he hopes the industry continues to "see us. That we're there, and we know how to do it. And just trust us, because sometimes we have to prove to them once, twice and three times that we are able to do it."

Alexander Skarsgård presented the hair and makeup award to Joe Dunckley for "Wicker" which required transforming the actor into a wooden man through an extensive prosthetics process. During his introduction, Skarsgård jokingly thanked Dunckley for allowing his lifelong dream of being made of wicker come true.

"At Wētā Workshop, we combine the art form of weaving with new methods of directly 3D printing prosthetic makeup, creating a weave that moved with Alexander's performance," Dunckley said. "That innovation came from collaboration. 80 people at Wētā Workshop contributed to this character. I'm proud of what we achieved together."

Anne Ross received the production design award for "The Debut," which was presented to her by the film's creator, Jesse Eisenberg. He recalled first working with Ross on the 2005 "The Squid and the Whale," where she asked everyone on set to bring in books to help fill the background of a scene.

"When I was making this new movie, ‘The Debut,' I wanted someone who would be able to go bigger in scope than the budget we had, and I thought I needed the person who collected those books," Eisenberg said. "I needed someone who would ask the cast and crew for books instead of just settling for a smaller bookshelf, and that is Anne. The way I think about working with Anne is that she is good at every single thing that I am not good at, and I trust her completely."

John Malkovich presented the directing accolade to Martin McDonagh for "Wild Horse Nine," recalling that he had previously turned down the filmmaker's offers to star in "A Behanding in Spokane" and "Seven Psychopaths" before finally accepting his latest film. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"By this point in the relationship, most people would take the hint," Malkovich joked in his introduction. "But Martin is a man who once wrote a character who cut off his own fingers just to prove a point. So thank God I didn't have a scheduling conflict when he asked me to be in ‘Wild Horse Nine.'"

During his acceptance speech, McDonagh praised Malkovich's "astonishing performance," citing it as "the main reason I'm up here tonight." He also told Variety that he would "love to be a small part" of helping the actor win his first Oscar.

"To watch him go up there and get it would be kind of cool! I'd be like a giddy kid," McDonagh said on the red carpet.

Scott Morris took home the editing prize for "Paper Tiger," which was presented by Miles Teller. In editing the James Gray film, Morris said he prioritized the characters, letting their mood guide the story.

"The cutting room is very much a place of trust and creative freedom. Together, we're working toward this common goal," Morris said in his acceptance speech. "It's this beautiful corroboration where we're on this journey of exploration. I'm so grateful that James [Gray] brought me into his world."

The final award of the night was presented to Raül Refree by Judeline for the score of "La Bola Negra."

"Raül gave the Spanish classic ‘Soldadito Español' a completely new meaning, moving away from its epic spirit to reveal something much more intimate: the sadness and loneliness of war," Judeline said in her introduction. "Not just one war, but any war… His music doesn't just accompany the images. It tells its own story."

Refree revealed he and directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — commonly known as Los Javis — discussed creating "La Bola Negra" for years, and the filmmakers asked him to "compose some music" in advance that they could use for inspiration while writing the script.

“Los Javis, they are very clever, and they give you all the space that you need to try to tell your own vision of the story,” Refree told Variety on the red carpet. “That made me feel super free to compose.”

The composer also teased that Calvo and Ambrossi already “have an idea” for their next project, and he trusts “they are going to make an incredible step forward.”
